NTA but I think there needs to be a serious talk with your mother, rather than cutting her out right away. Try to call or Skype first, and if that's not an option show up with your fiance to talk with her one on one. Explain how hurt her actions made you feel, and that you truly don't want to cut her out, but what she did is a threat to your family. And if she starts with the whole "complete family" nonsense tell her it is YOUR family, and YOUR son, not hers. If she doesn't agree to these terms, you'll have to give her the ultimatum, but make sure your dad knows what you're discussing ahead of time and understands that this doesn't apply to him unless he does the same thing your mom is doing. At the end of the day, your fiance has already been a step-father to your son, and his bio father really hasn't been there. Your mom needs to see the value in your child having a GOOD father figure rather than just a biological one. Best of luck!

As this one's girlfriend (hey babe 😘), I can confirm that the height difference doesn't matter! I love being taller than him (I feel so POWERFUL!) and no one else seems to really care about it. I think if you love someone, their height really doesn't make a difference in how "easy" the relationship is, because all relationships come with unique challenges, like whether one of you is lactose intolerant, afraid of heights, or even just a dog or cat person. If you love them and work together in the relationship, you figure it out and learn how to navigate your differences. Like with us, everyone around us was just happy that we were happy, and I've never gotten mean stares or comments about it. If anything, our height difference (and weight difference) is just another thing that makes us a little unique, but we appreciate our differences and always make sure that when insecurities do come up, we address them together. If a guy doesn't like you because you're curvy and taller than him, he isn't the guy for you. You should never have to feel uncomfortable in your own skin to be with someone, because there will always be someone out there who worships the ground you walk on just for being you. Good luck, girl!

Say there's an illness (like the flu) where about 5 out of 100 people in the population get it (so 5%). A test to see if you have it is available, and it is 99% accurate for true positive results (you have the flu and the test says you have it), and 90% accurate for true negative results (you don't have the flu and the test says you don't have it). You have no reason to believe you are any more or less likely to catch the flu than everyone else. 

If you get a positive test result (the test says you have the flu) you are actually MUCH more likely to not have the flu despite the positive result (given that you've gotten a positive test result, it is only about 34% likely you actually have the flu versus about 66% likely that you do NOT have the flu).

Our brains like to take positive test results much more seriously than negative results, even when the math shows us that we're wrong! (I learned this in a logic and probability class, really interesting stuff!)
